core_claim: arXiv was built in 1991 as a physics preprint server, but the post-ChatGPT AI boom has turned it into a computer-science archive — CS is now 42.5% of everything posted and crossed 50% of all submissions in a single month (May 2025).

edt_01.label: Hook — a physics server that isn't physics anymore
edt_01.title: A physics server that isn't physics anymore
edt_01.editorial_notes: 50.8% (May 2025) and 33.8% (Jan 2022) must be exact — the single-month majority is the entire hook. Interactive should let the reader guess CS's current share before revealing it, driven by ana_16's monthly series.

edt_02.title: From two papers to three million
edt_02.editorial_notes: ana_01 chart may run the full history (full-history file is NOT truncated at 2025-10). Image = founder portrait det_media_02 (Paul Ginsparg). Keep this short — it is backdrop, not the lead.

edt_03.title: The four categories that ate arXiv
edt_03.editorial_notes: Top-4 = 25.3%; cs.LG = 134,903 (largest single category). Optional image det_media_03 (Geoffrey Hinton) to put a face on the AI boom — Designer's call. Do NOT sum mirrored category pairs in the ranking chart (ana_23).

edt_04.label: Not growth — a takeover
edt_04.title: Not growth — a takeover
edt_04.editorial_notes: This is the conceptual turn: other fields grew ~20% but LOST share because CS grew 1.85x. CS rose 36.7%->46.7%; physics fell 34.9%->28.9%. Group-level shares are the clean unit. Interactive could let readers compare a CS category vs a flat physics one over time. All charts here end at 2025-09.

edt_05.title: How fast it happened
edt_05.editorial_notes: cs.AI 2.87x, cs.CL 2.65x. May 2023 = first 20k month, ~6 months after ChatGPT. ana_12 chart ends at 2025-09; ana_03 (full-history peaks) may run to tail. Interactive option: scrub a category's monthly curve to feel the bend post-2022.

edt_06.label: Demand kept pace — and then some
edt_06.title: Readers came too
edt_06.editorial_notes: MUST show or omit the 2024 gap (downloads file jumps 2023-11 -> 2025-01); never imply a 2024 collapse. r=0.94. downloads/submission 299->569->1889. No non-text media needed — a clean dual-axis trend chart carries it.

edt_07.label: Still climbing — and the limits of the data
edt_07.title: Still climbing
edt_07.editorial_notes: CS +21.7% YoY through last complete month — no slowdown visible. The 2025-10 ~95% drop is a truncation artifact, NOT a crash; this must be stated in prose. End on the open question (can arXiv stay the venue for AI), not a summary. ana_22 chart ends at 2025-09; never plot the partial 2025-10 for category/archive data.
